literal: Ruin knowing-not, ruined place-at-even, wealth diminishing-not country, say-they, of countries head.
translation: They say the best of countries is one that knows no ruin, and whose wealth does not diminish even when disaster strikes.
modern: அழிவைச் சந்திக்காததும், ஒருவேளை அழிவு நேர்ந்தாலும் தன் வளம் குறையாததுமான நாடே நாடுகளுள் தலைசிறந்தது என்று கூறுவர்.
explanation: This couplet defines the resilience of an ideal nation. The phrase "கேடு அறியா" means the country naturally avoids destruction. However, the text adds "கெட்ட இடத்தும்" (even when ruined), acknowledging that unforeseen disasters might still strike. In such events, a truly great country is one whose resources ("வளம்") do not diminish ("குன்றா"). The word "தலை" (head) is used metaphorically to mean the chief or the best among all countries.
